Are you looking for an opportunity to truly make a difference? Do you want to join a collaborative, mission-driven team that protects the planet, strengthens communities, and supports businesses when they need it most? Crisis Communications Manager
Central London
If you can name a ship, it’s probably because it sank. We work to keep our clients’ vessels off the list of ships you’ve heard of.
Navigate Response, a Witt O’Brien’s company, is the strongest global crisis communications network specializing in the international shipping, port and offshore industries; headquartered in London, Houston and Singapore, we operate a global network of 45 offices in 30 countries around the world.

Excellent (and we do mean excellent) writer

Confident and polished public speaker

Knowledge of commercial shipping and/or crisis communications experience

Experience delivering senior level media (or other relevant) training programs

Who are we?
Howden is a global insurance group with employee ownership at its heart. Together, we have pushed the boundaries of insurance. We are united by a shared passion and no-limits mindset, and our strength lies in our ability to collaborate as a powerful international team comprised of 24,000 employees spanning over 56 countries.
People join Howden for many different reasons, but they stay for the same one: our culture. It’s what sets us apart, and the reason our employees have been turning down headhunters for years. Whatever your priorities – work / life balance, career progression, sustainability, volunteering – you’ll find like-minded people driving change at Howden.
With a no limits approach, we can rise to any challenge. Whatever the question, the concern, or the risk, we can get the right people in a room and find the right answer. Our collective power is also helping us to change the insurance narrative – doing right by our clients while using insurance as a tool to build resilience for individuals, businesses and communities. From pro bono work to insuring COVID-19 vaccine development to de-risking the carbon market, we’re using our skills, knowledge, and networks to make a difference and speed positive change in the world around us.
We are actively looking for a Commercial Account Executive to join our Howden Consumer & Local Commercial team. Our local Commercial team have grown rapidly over the last 14 years’, and we now have over 200 people within the team across the UK. In this role you will be responsible for building rapport with new and existing clients, who could range from sole traders, through to the MD/CEO of a large organisation, and working closely with the Branch Manager to achieve objectives.
About you:
• You will have experience winning new business and building long lasting relationships with B2B clients.
• You must have a passion for developing business through marketing, community engagement, networking, client meetings, just to name a few – the stronger our presence in the market, the more successful you will be.
• You will be tenacious and have a business curiosity, as this will allow you to identify and explore new business opportunities to drive the best possible outcome for our clients
• You are willing to learn, as every day will be different. This is a great opportunity to progress your career as a Commercial Account Executive and become further your professional qualifications.
• You are consultative, have the ability to question effectively and will be an active listener, you will take the time to fully understand client requirements and be able to advise on products and solutions – always identifying opportunities, but more importantly, looking for a ‘path to yes’
Rewards:
We believe that great work and dedication should be rewarded, that’s why we offer:
• 22 days holiday (plus bank holidays), increasing through length of service
• A set of core benefits, designed with your health and financial protection in mind:
• Life Assurance up to 4x salary, protecting your loved ones in case the worst should happen
• Income protection, guaranteeing an income for up to 5 years in the event of an illness or injury
• Contributory pension scheme – 5% employer contribution and 5% employee contribution
• Access to a Healthcare Cashplan, which gives you access to a variety of health related benefits
• Access to a host of lifestyle and financial benefits that you can choose from:
• Discounts on gym membership across the UK
• Salary sacrifice schemes – Travel Insurance, Cycle to Work, Car leasing, Technology purchase
• Access to a range of insurance polices through Howden at discounted rates
• Access to hundreds of high-street retailer discounts
What do we offer in return?
A career that you define. At Howden, we value diversity – there is no one Howden type. Instead, we’re looking for individuals who share the same values as us:
•
Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new
•
We support each other in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges
•
We are determined to make a positive difference at work and beyond
Reasonable adjustments
We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations at Howden to ensure that our positions align well with your needs.  Besides the usual adjustments such as software, IT, and office setups, we can also accommodate other changes such as flexible hours* or hybrid working*.
If you're excited by this role but have some doubts about whether it’s the right fit for you, send us your application – if your profile fits the role’s criteria, we will be in touch to assist in helping to get you set up with any reasonable adjustments you may require.
*Not all positions can accommodate changes to working hours or locations. Reach out to your Recruitment Partner if you want to know more.

Job Description
Job Title: Credit Risk, Leveraged Finance
Corporate Title: Associate
Location: London
Company Overview:
At Bank of America, we are guided by a common purpose to help make financial lives better through the power of every connection.  Responsible Growth is how we run our company and how we deliver for our clients, teammates, communities and shareholders every day.
One of the keys to driving Responsible Growth is being a great place to work for our teammates around the world. We’re devoted to being a diverse and inclusive workplace for everyone. Bank of America believes both in the importance of working together and offering flexibility to our employees. We use a multi-faceted approach for flexibility, depending on the various roles in our organization.
Working at Bank of America will give you a great career with opportunities to learn, grow and make an impact, along with the power to make a difference. Join us!
Location Overview:
Our London office is based just a stone’s throw from the magnificent St. Paul’s Cathedral on bustling King Edward Street. Here you’ll find modern workspaces and a state-of-the-art auditorium space. In addition, we’re proud to host an onsite restaurant that shares our commitment to sustainability by providing delicious seasonal menus which have been created with the planet in mind. Make sure to take time for yourself and head up to our rooftop terrace and take in the spectacular views across London. Finally, your physical wellness is well-catered for with our onsite gym facilities and medical centre.
Role Description:
Leveraged Finance Credit supports the development, due diligence, approval and implementation of leveraged transactions for corporate and financial sponsors.  Typical transactions include leveraged buyouts, mergers and acquisitions, refinancings, recapitalizations, and restructurings.
Responsibilities
•
Work closely with senior members of the department, building experience in the leveraged finance market and provide support at all stages of the credit life cycle.
•
Assist with the review of due diligence, assessment of forecasts and/or building of models, and writing of credit memorandum.
•
Provide guidance regarding drivers of loan returns and profitability.
•
Establish and maintain a deep understanding of the portfolio at the client, industry, and macro level in order to assess risk and form considered opinions.
•
Maintain timely and accurate monitoring (risk ratings, financial reports, compliance certificates, forecasts, and annual reviews).
•
Ensure adherence to prevailing credit policy and procedures.
•
Develop an understanding of core documentation across loans and derivatives.
•
Have exposure to the full Global Banking & Global Markets product spectrum with engagement across multiple stakeholders, including Leveraged Finance, Financial Sponsors, Investment Banking, Corporate Banking, Sales & Trading, Legal, and Risk.
•
Participate in strategic projects to support both team and business goals.
Skills that will help:
•
Relevant experience with a major financial institution; preferably being on or having completed a graduate scheme or equivalent program.
•
Corporate credit background, with leveraged finance experience preferred but not compulsory.
•
Credit risk awareness and understanding of risk drivers on appetite, exposures and ratings.
•
Able to extract and assess information relating to credit quality, analytically curious.
•
Positive and proactive ‘can do’ attitude with a willingness to learn and adapt.
•
Competent with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
Bank of America
Good conduct and sound judgment is crucial to our long term success. It’s important that all employees in the organisation understand the expected standards of conduct and how we manage conduct risk. Individual accountability and an ownership mind-set are the cornerstones of our Code of Conduct and are at the heart of managing risk well.
We are an equal opportunities employer, and ensure that no applicant is subject to less favourable treatment on the grounds of gender, gender identity, marital status, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origins, age, sexual orientation, socio-economic background, responsibilities for dependants, physical or mental disability. The Bank selects candidates for interview based on their skills, qualifications and experience.
We strive to ensure that our recruitment processes are accessible for all candidates and encourage any candidates to tell us about any adjustment requirements.

If you currently work for Brown-Forman, please apply by clicking the Careers icon on the Workday portal.
For best results, use Google Chrome to view this page.
Meaningful Work From Day One
Our business in the UK (BFBE) & Ireland are growing and diverse. This role is responsible for Brown-Forman’s UK (BFBE) & Ireland US GAAP and Nordics &Baltics third party markets local statutory accounting. It ensures the accuracy and integrity of Brown-Forman’s financial records with respect to (a) US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), (b) local accounting standards, and (c) all relevant tax regimes, including US and local corporate income tax and indirect taxes (Excise and VAT). This role will assist the Regional controller Europe in providing accounting and controlling advice on potential transactions or business changes. It will also serve as a business partner to senior corporate and divisional management by communicating quantitative and qualitative information in a clear and accurate manner to support management decision making. This role will lead an accounting team which is made up of managers, senior accountants, accountants and analysts in various locations.
The working style for this role is 4 days a week out of our modern office in Fitzrovia in central London with Fridays working from home.
What You Can Expect
Integrity of Financial Records
● Responsible for ensuring all financial records are maintained in accordance with US GAAP and local statutory regulations in a timely and accurate manner.
● This position addresses tight deadlines and a multitude of accounting and tax compliance activities (Excise, VAT) including month end closing, preparation and submission of various tax returns and legal statutory audit.
● Review and analyze balance sheet reconciliations, reasonableness and provide explanation to their fluctuations
● Own the rebates processing process and ensure their accuracy and timeliness. Collaborate closely with Commercial and GBS Pricing and Rebates team on accurate accruals and releases and provide a robust discounts/ rebates analytics in the balance sheet
● Responsible for the timely and accurate completion of our internal SOX Narratives around key processes.
● Partner with GBS CCCA Process Lead to lead the CCCA team to ensure all reports are delivered on time, customers overdue amounts are being investigated and promptly action on
● Partner with GBS ITP Process Lead to ensure Accounts payable and T&E managed timely and with expected accuracy
● Partner with Tax Manager to lead and complete any HMRC due diligence exercises (inquiry/audit), HMRC business risk review, Senior Accounting Officer (SAO) attestation, maintenance of the risk assessment and controls matrix (RACM)

The Senior Data Product Manager owns a defined area of the EPH product estate – the attributes that enable us to sell a product, from what it's called to how it's identified and how it's sold. Join us and make a difference when it matters most!
At Bard, we are committed to ensuring the quality, safety, and compliance of the medicines supplied to patients worldwide. As part of our continued commitment to operational excellence and regulatory compliance, we are seeking a Sample Management Coordinator to support the efficient administration, tracking, shipment, and disposition of analytical samples across Bard laboratories and external European testing facilities.
This role plays a critical part in supporting batch release activities by ensuring analytical samples and associated documentation are managed accurately, securely, and within defined timelines.
Role Summary
The Sample Management Coordinator is responsible for the end-to-end management of analytical samples required for product testing and release activities.
The role ensures all samples are correctly logged, tracked, shipped, and accounted for within established timelines while maintaining compliance with GMP, GDP, import/export regulations, and company procedures. The post-holder will act as a key liaison between Bard laboratories, external analytical laboratories, logistics providers, and internal stakeholders to support timely batch disposition.
The successful candidate will be responsible for maintaining sample traceability, managing analytical documentation, coordinating shipments of controlled substances and reference standards, and ensuring the integrity of inventory and laboratory management systems.
Role and Responsibilities
Sample Management & Logistics
• Manage the receipt, registration, storage, tracking, and shipment of analytical samples and reference materials.
• Ensure all sample management activities are performed in accordance with approved Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), GMP requirements, and company policies.
• Maintain accurate records within Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS) and Oracle inventory systems.
• Ensure full traceability and accountability of all analytical samples throughout their lifecycle.
• Coordinate weekly and ad hoc sample shipments to European and external laboratory partners.
• Liaise with courier providers and laboratory personnel to ensure secure transportation and custody of analytical samples, including Schedule 2 controlled substances.
• Monitor sample inventories and maintain appropriate stock levels of reference standards, consumables, chemicals, and laboratory materials.
• Escalate risks, delays, or discrepancies that may impact testing schedules or batch release activities.
Documentation & Regulatory Compliance
• Prepare, review, and maintain all documentation required for domestic and international sample shipments.
• Ensure import and export licences are obtained, maintained, renewed, and decommissioned as required.
• Generate and manage commercial invoices, shipping documentation, and export declarations.
• Maintain Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS), Certificates of Analysis (CoA), and other supporting documentation.
• Prepare Letters of No Objection and regulatory documentation where required by importing territories.
• Ensure compliance with controlled drug regulations and international shipping requirements.
• Support regulatory inspections and audits by maintaining accurate and inspection-ready records.
• Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, reviewed appropriately, and retained in accordance with data integrity requirements.
Laboratory Coordination & Sample Scheduling
• Schedule analytical sample dispatches to support laboratory testing priorities and optimize analytical cycle times.
• Coordinate with internal and external laboratories to ensure samples are received and tested within agreed timelines.
• Support laboratory planning activities by prioritizing shipments based on batch release requirements and production schedules.
• Assist laboratories in maintaining First-In-First-Out (FIFO) testing priorities through effective sample scheduling.
• Communicate critical testing requirements, territory-specific testing needs, and changing priorities to laboratory partners in a timely manner.
Analytical Data & Batch Support
• Review Certificates of Analysis received from testing laboratories and ensure accurate entry into LIMS.
• Verify analytical documentation is complete, accurate, and aligned with current approved specifications.
• Ensure external laboratories are working with current analytical methods, specifications, and approved procedures.
• Support the timely completion of analytical testing activities required for product disposition and release.
• Assist with data reconciliation activities to ensure accurate sample accountability and test completion status.
Performance & Continuous Improvement
• Monitor and report key performance indicators, including sample cycle times, shipment performance, and laboratory turnaround metrics.
• Produce monthly performance reports and operational metrics.
• Identify opportunities to improve sample handling, transportation efficiency, documentation processes, and laboratory coordination.
• Support continuous improvement initiatives aimed at reducing cycle times and improving operational efficiency.
• Participate in problem-solving and root cause investigations relating to sample management and logistics activities.
Health, Safety & Compliance
• Adhere to all company Health & Safety, security, environmental, and quality requirements.
• Handle controlled substances, reference materials, chemicals, and laboratory samples in accordance with approved procedures.
• Ensure all activities are conducted in compliance with GMP, GxP, GDP, and regulatory requirements.
• Promote a culture of quality, compliance, and continuous improvement.
• Undertake any other reasonable duties required to support laboratory operations, product quality, and patient supply.
Qualifications
Education
Minimum Required
• Minimum of 5 GCSEs (Grade C / Level 4 or above), including Mathematics and English, or equivalent qualifications.
Preferred
• A-Level qualifications, ideally in a scientific discipline, or equivalent vocational qualification.
• Degree or higher education qualification in Science, Supply Chain, Logistics, Business Administration, or a related field.
Experience
Minimum Required
• Experience working within a logistics, administrative, inventory management, warehouse, laboratory support, or regulated operational environment.
• Experience managing documentation and records with a high level of accuracy.
• Experience coordinating activities involving internal and external stakeholders.
Preferred
• Experience within the pharmaceutical, healthcare, laboratory, or life sciences industry.
• Experience using Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS).

As a Test Systems Technical Lead, you will be responsible for the technical direction, definition, and delivery of test system solutions across Power Distribution and Controls programs. Working as part of an Integrated Product Development Team (IPDT), you will lead the full test systems lifecycle from initial requirements capture through design, implementation, verification, release, and in-service support. You will demonstrate strong technical leadership, collaborate closely with Program and Engineering Project Managers, and provide guidance, coaching, and mentoring to engineers in the test systems team.
Job Description
Roles and Responsibilities

Own the technical solution for test systems in your product/project area, ensuring alignment to customer, regulatory, and internal requirements.  Lead the full Test Systems life cycle from concept and requirements definition through design, implementation, verification, formal release, and in-service support. Execute requirements, design, implementation, and verification using sound engineering principles, adhering to business standards, procedures, and program requirements. Ensure test equipment solutions are suitable for qualification, EMC, system verification, and production support, in line with DO-160, MIL-STD-461 and similar standards.
2. Technical Leadership
Own the technical direction and accountability for test systems within your project to meet customer and derived requirements. Monitor and steer the technical solution, ensuring rigor in design and technical reviews for your test solution. Collaborate with the Designated Technical Authority (DTA) to ensure test system architectures and strategies are aligned to the overall product architecture. Engage SMEs and Chief Engineer’s Office as needed to resolve complex technical issues, de-risk solutions, and ensure compliance with internal design guidelines. Ensure adherence to project plans, company and industry standards, and appropriate application of DTC (Design to Cost) and DFM (Design for Manufacture) / DFT (Design for Test) principles for test solutions.
3. Budget / Schedule / Scope Support
Support the Control Account Manager (CAM) and EPM in delivering the technical solution to the agreed scope, schedule, and budget for your project. Protect against internal and external scope creep for the test system, identifying potential changes early and supporting mitigation. Clearly communicate technical expectations to the engineering team, including definition of done, entry/exit criteria, and required deliverables. Support work package planning (e.g., rolling wave planning, milestones, and estimates) and provide input to technical metrics to monitor progress and health of test activities. Provide timely technical inputs to program reviews, Toll Gates, forecast updates, and risk & opportunity reviews as requested by EPM/PM.
4. Cross-functional Collaboration and Customer Interface
Act as the engineering interface to Program Management on test systems topics, clearly articulating technical direction, risks, and decisions. Liaise and interface with Systems, Hardware, Software, Manufacturing, Sustaining, Quality, Supply Chain, and Lab Operations to ensure integrated and robust test solutions. Support Program Manager and EPM in customer and certification discussions related to test system capability, coverage, readiness, and evidence. Ensure alignment and coordination with Manufacturing Program Manager (Launch Leader) and production test stakeholders regarding test strategy, manufacturability, and transition to production test environments.
5. Governance, Documentation, and Compliance
Assure proper documentation of technical data generated for test systems in line with engineering policies, configuration control, and quality requirements. Ensure test system requirements, design artefacts, verification evidence, and configuration baselines are defined, maintained, and traceable. Participate as presenter or reviewer in technical, design, and program reviews (including CEO/DTA reviews where applicable), ensuring issues, risks, and lessons learned are captured and addressed. Support change management activities for test systems, providing technical impact assessments for scope/schedule changes and feeding into program BCRs as required.
6. People Leadership, Coaching and Behaviours
Provide technical guidance and leadership to engineers and technicians working on test systems, ensuring clarity of priorities, deliverables, and standards. Coach, mentor, and train less experienced engineers, actively building technical capability and succession in the test systems community. Model and reinforce GE Leadership Behaviours – Act with Humility, Lead with Transparency, Deliver with Focus – and the supporting core values of Leading, Influencing, and Collaborating. Demonstrate and promote key team behaviours, including risk identification and mitigation, proactive information sharing, collaborative decision making, constructive feedback, problem solving, and driving Lean and cost out. Provide timely communications on significant technical issues or developments and use the defined escalation paths (Tech Lead/CAM → EPM → Subsection Manager/PMO → PM → senior leadership) where resolution is blocked or risks escalate.
Required Qualifications
Degree in Electrical, Electronic, or Software Engineering, or equivalent knowledge and experience. Significant experience in test system design, development, and integration, including hardware/software integration for complex systems, ideally in aviation or other high integrity/safety-critical environments. Demonstrated experience in qualification and EMC test equipment design, with working knowledge/awareness of DO-160, MIL-STD-461 or equivalent environmental and EMC standards.
Proven technical leadership experience delivering solutions to agreed scope, schedule, cost, and quality, preferably as a Technical Lead, CAM, or equivalent within a project environment. Strong problem-solving and solution-building skills, with the ability to break down complex problems, identify options, and drive to resolution.
Excellent communication skills, able to clearly convey complex technical topics to engineering teams, program management, customers, and leadership. Evidence of independent and sound technical judgement, including identifying when to escalate and when to seek DTA/CEO guidance.

Join Leonardo at a pivotal time of growth, where your engineering leadership will play a key role in shaping and delivering future capabilities.
Leonardo is seeking motivated and experienced Project Engineering Leads (PELs) to join our Electronic Warfare Line of Business within the Integrated Mission Solutions (IMS) sector. This is a permanent opportunity to support the continued growth of the Mission Support Products Integrated Project Team (IPT).
As a Project Engineering Lead, you will report to the Project Engineering Manager (PEM) and work closely with the Chief Engineer to provide engineering leadership and management across a range of programmes. You will be responsible for identifying, developing, delivering, and supporting technical solutions that meet the needs of our customers and end users.
The role combines both contract delivery and business-winning activities, providing engineering direction, leadership, and management across multiple customers and stakeholders.
Based at our Luton office, this position offers hybrid working, with a nominal requirement of 2-3 days per week on site. There will also be opportunities to travel within the UK, collaborating with Leonardo teams, customers, end users, and industry partners, with occasional overseas travel as required.
What you’ll do as a Project Engineering Lead:
As a Project Engineering Lead, you will be responsible for the day-to-day engineering management of projects, ensuring delivery against technical, schedule, and budget commitments.
Typical responsibilities include:
• Leading the engineering and engineering bid activities of projects, ensuring technical excellence, effective schedule management, and budget control.
• Managing cross-site, multi-disciplinary engineering teams, ensuring roles and responsibilities are clearly defined and understood.
• Developing and supporting engineering team members through mentoring, coaching, objective setting, and performance appraisals.
• Building strong and effective relationships with customers and industry partners to successfully deliver project capabilities.
• Establishing and maintaining effective communication across the Engineering IPT, Project Managers, IPT Leads, and Functional Heads.
• Working closely with the Systems Design Authority to ensure visibility of technical progress, risks, issues, and mitigation plans.
• Ensuring design solutions meet end-user requirements, are reliable, fully documented, and operate effectively within the intended environment.
• Ensuring solutions align with the wider business area roadmap and strategic direction.
• Managing project configuration and change control activities to maximise design reuse and maintain product integrity.
• Supporting supplier management activities and contributing to make-or-buy decisions for project deliverables.
What we need from you:
You really must have:
• Engineering Management experience across multiple phases of the engineering lifecycle.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to provide clear direction and leadership to engineering teams.
• The ability to develop clear, concise, and achievable engineering plans
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Experience in schedule management and budget control.
• The ability to communicate effectively with a broad range of stakeholders across multiple locations.
• Strong leadership capability combined with excellent team-working skills.
• Commercial awareness and an understanding of business drivers
• The ability to manage complex situations, exercise sound judgement, and balance competing priorities.
• A willingness to travel within the UK and occasionally overseas
It would be nice if you had:
• Experience within the military or defence domain.
• Knowledge of Agile methodologies and delivery practices.
• Experience using DevOps-based tools and environments.
• Experience in problem definition, requirements elicitation, and software product definition.
• Knowledge of the development and certification of airborne equipment.
• Experience supporting New Product Introduction (NPI) activities.
• Experience managing or outsourcing complex engineering work packages.
• An engineering or scientific degree qualification, or equivalent experience.
This is not an exhaustive list, and we would still like to hear from you even if you do not meet every requirement. At Leonardo, we recognise that potential, attitude, and a willingness to learn are just as important as experience. If you are passionate about engineering leadership and want to contribute to cutting-edge mission solutions, we encourage you to apply.
Security Clearance
This role is subject to pre-employment screening in line with the UK Government’s Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS). An additional range of Personnel Security Controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV) may apply, this could include meeting the eligibility requirements for The Security Check (SC) or Developed Vetting (DV). For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting

At Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We offer a comprehensive, company-funded benefits package that supports your wellbeing, career development, and work–life balance. Whether you're looking to grow professionally, care for your health, or plan for the future, we’re here to help you thrive.

• Never Stop Learning: Free access to 4,000+ online courses via Coursera and LinkedIn Learning.
• Refer a friend: Receive a financial reward through our referral programme.
• Tailored Perks: Spend up to £500 annually on flexible benefits including private healthcare, dental, family cover, tech & lifestyle discounts, gym memberships and more.
• Flexible working: Flexible hours with hybrid working options. For part time opportunities, please talk to us about what might be possible for this role.
For a full list of our company benefits please visit our website.

Welcome to the world of land-based gaming. At Light & Wonder, it’s all about the games, and our Gaming team builds cutting-edge technology, products, and content for the most iconic casinos and operators across the globe.

Develop high-quality game content using Unity, C++ and C#.
•
Design, implement, and maintain game features that deliver engaging player experiences.

Write clean, efficient, and maintainable code in line with established engineering standards and best practices.
•
Contribute to technical design discussions, helping shape software architecture and implementation approaches.
•
Take ownership of software components throughout the development lifecycle, from concept and design through to testing and release.
•
Investigate, troubleshoot, and resolve software defects, performance issues, and technical challenges.
•
Optimise game performance, stability, and maintainability across multiple projects.
•
Collaborate closely with artists, game designers, mathematicians, QA engineers, and fellow developers to deliver high-quality content.
•
Participate in code reviews, sharing constructive feedback and helping maintain quality across the codebase.
•
Support and mentor junior engineers, providing technical guidance and encouraging professional development.
•
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, identifying opportunities to enhance development processes, tools, and engineering practices.
•
Share knowledge across the team and help foster a collaborative, high-performing engineering culture.
What You'll Bring
•
Commercial experience developing software in C++, including the ability to understand, debug, and maintain complex codebases.
•
Experience developing games using the Unity game engine.
•
Strong capability in C# and object-oriented programming principles.
•
Excellent programming knowledge supported by solid software engineering fundamentals.
•
The ability to design, develop, debug, and maintain robust, scalable software solutions.
•
Experience delivering software throughout the full development lifecycle.
•
A solid understanding of software architecture, design patterns, and engineering best practices.
•
Strong analytical thinking and a practical approach to problem-solving.
•
Experience working effectively within multidisciplinary teams.
•
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to share knowledge, provide feedback, and support colleagues.
•
Experience mentoring, coaching, or developing other engineers.
•
A proactive, organised approach with the ability to manage workload independently and deliver to agreed deadlines.
•
A collaborative mindset and commitment to team success.
Qualifications
Degree or equivalent experience in Software Engineering
How You'll Grow
•
See your work reach players around the world through market-leading gaming content and products.
•
Develop your technical expertise by working alongside experienced engineers, designers, artists, and mathematicians in a highly collaborative studio environment.
•
Expand your impact through mentoring, technical leadership, and helping shape the next generation of gaming experiences at Light & Wonder.
What Can We Offer You?

Annual performance bonus
•
25 days' holiday plus bank holidays
•
1 day paid leave to work on charitable projects
•
1 day paid for personal celebration e.g. birthdays
•
Half Day for Health, encouraging you to take time away for you and your wellbeing
•
Up to 8% employer pension contributions
•
A reward platform offering cycle to work, shopping and lifestyle discounts/cashback
•
Remote GP access alongside a wellbeing platform
•
Private Medical Insurance
•
Elective benefits including Tastecard, travel insurance, dental insurance and Give As You Earn
•
Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)
•
A collaborative studio culture with regular social events, team nights out, and board-game evenings

Job Description
Are you passionate about making a difference and helping others?
Would you like to work in a role that puts the customer at the heart of everything we do, making a genuine positive impact?
Then consider the role of Careers Coach at Reed in Partnership!
This role is office based, but will involve travel across Norfolk also.
Who we are:
Reed's Employability Division aims to positively transform lives by helping individuals who are unemployed, economically inactive, or facing challenges such as health conditions, disabilities, or caring responsibilities to find sustainable employment. Through a wide range of tailored support services including one-to-one careers guidance, CV writing, interview preparation, and skills training, we have supported over 250,000 people on their journey into work.
Jobs Guarantee is a mandatory programme for 18-24 year olds who have been on Universal Credit for 18 months or more, providing a fully subsidised six month paid job of up to 25 hours per week at minimum wage.
What is this role about?
Jobs Guarantee is a mandatory programme for 18-24 year olds who have been on Universal Credit for 18 months or more, providing a fully subsidised six month paid job of up to 25 hours per week at minimum wage.
A Careers Coach will use a variety of techniques including effective diagnosis, individual and group coaching, and maximising on any participant funding available to prepare them for employment, and access local education or training opportunities. A Careers Coach is also responsible for conducting outreach in the community, building relationships with referral partners (DWP/JCP), and attending local events (e.g. job fairs) to generate referrals.  They will also engage with local employers, training providers, and other key partners to source suitable opportunities that align with the participants’ goals.
Just some of your day-to-day responsibilities include:
• Identifying each participants skills and strengths, and suitable training, placements and volunteering opportunities.
• Providing support with CV preparation, job-searching, and interview skills.
• Conducting outreach activity such as running events and sessions at community organisations, attending job fair events and other promotional activity.
• Facilitating group training courses and workshops according to their needs.
• Employer engagement and stakeholder management with the JCP.

A generous base salary (pro-rata for part time), and great flexibility with your working schedule, we offer training, development and progression opportunities. You will have access to the range of Reed in Partnership benefits, which include:
• 25 days annual leave (pro-rata for part time) plus statutory bank holidays
• Reed Pension Scheme
• Award Winning Management & Leadership training
• Professional & Personal Development Funds
• Bi-annual pay reviews
• Plus much more that can be found on our website
• With the chance to dramatically make a difference to the local community, this role offers immense job satisfaction.
To be successful in this role, we are looking for someone with:
Essential Attainments
• Experience of working in a customer facing environment (i.e. Customer Services, Hospitality, Social Care, Customer Services, Sales)
• Experience of working in a performance target driven environment
• Willingness to travel locally, and access to own vehicle (e.g. to meet customers/employers).
• A minimum of 2 A-Levels or an equivalent Level 3 Diploma.
• GCSE English Language at a minimum of a Grade B (or equivalent Level 2 qualification).
Desirable Attainments:
• Experience of working in a fast-paced environment.  Examples of such experience may include working as a Holiday Representative or Recruitment Consultant, etc.
• Experience of and exposure to client groups.  These client groups may include incapacity benefit claimants, single parents, those with criminal records, mental health groups, ex-services, specific ethnic minority or faith groups and those with specific disabilities.
• Direct previous experience of a similar role. Roles considered to be similar include the role of Employment Adviser on a welfare to work contract or a publicly funded service.
• Degree or relevant qualification. Degree topics may include psychology, sociology, and social care/science. Relevant qualifications would include Information Advice and Guidance NVQs, Brokerage Standard, Social Work qualifications or qualifications relating to work with the specific client groups this role will involve
• Level 3 or 4 NVQ in Advice & Guidance or Education & Training
• Fluency in community languages. Community languages may include Cantonese, Mandarin, Hindi, Urdu, Punjabi, Somali, Vietnamese, Dari, Yoruba, Turkish, French, Spanish, Albanian, Arabic, Bengali, Farsi, Guajarati, Polish, Serbian and Greek (Dependent on programme).

There are NO limits to your career: come shape the future and be part of a truly unique global culture at OutSystems!
The Senior Account Executive at OutSystems will add new logos, manage the entire sales process from discovery to close, and will leverage his or her network to gain access to selling opportunities.
The ideal candidate will have over 10 years of experience in a direct sales role and will have the ability to partner with System Integrators, Channel, and Alliance partners. He/She will have excellent communication and problem-solving skills along with the ability to be self-driven and to work independently.
What You Will Lead/Do or Key Responsibilities
•
Uncover and manage new selling opportunities in a geographic territory
•
Call on and develop relationships with C-level executives across business and IT units for named accounts
•
Execute a sales process that validates and qualifies the technical and business requirements of the customer in order to close the business

Articulate the value proposition and be familiar with ROI and TCO tools at a business level to provide to Business Stakeholders
•
Negotiate contracts, up-sell and cross-sell, build customer rapport
•
Achieve sales quotas in a territory on a quarterly and annual basis by developing a sales strategy in the allocated territory with a target prospect list, and a regional sales plan to include selling with and through partners.

Prospect, effectively qualify, and develop new sales opportunities and ongoing revenue streams from new and existing accounts.
•
Work with Global and local SIs and Channel partners to promote OutSystems solutions
Qualifications / What You Need To Succeed
•
Bachelor’s Degree (or equivalent experience)
•
10+ years of direct and indirect selling experience within the enterprise software space and 3+ years within the application & application development space, SaaS.PaaS and Cloud offerings.
•
Strong technical sales background with the ability to explain the business value to executives, experienced managing complex sales processes.
•
Experience/ Success with named account selling model
•
Proven track record of partnering with Global and Local System Integrators and Channel Partners.
The Longer Story:
OutSystems enables enterprise teams to build AI-powered applications and agents that reduce manual work, streamline internal operations, and accelerate impact. A proven low-code foundation combined with agentic AI and AI app generation capabilities empowers teams to move up to 10x faster with the assurance of security, scalability, and governance built in.
As the future becomes agentic, our customers need us now more than ever. AI has opened the door to extraordinary possibilities—but inside the enterprise, things are moving fast and feeling chaotic. Some early adopters are making progress in production, but for many, AI tools are sprawling without governance, data isn’t ready, and talent isn’t there yet. Enterprises are still drowning in application backlogs and struggling with legacy systems. But with the right platform, AI doesn’t have to add to the chaos. It can become the breakthrough that brings clarity—and drives real, enterprise-wide impact. At OutSystems, we’ve built that platform, providing the tools necessary for enterprises to overcome these hurdles.
We are looking for passionate, talented, and motivated people to join us in helping our customers build, deploy, and scale apps and agents—fast, helping them accelerate innovation while enabling secure, governed human-AI collaboration.
OutSystems is a truly global company, with more than 850,000 developer community members, 1,700 employees, more than 500 partners, and thousands of active customers in over 75 countries and across 21 industries. Founded in 2001, OutSystems has offices in the United States, United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Portugal, Germany, the UAE, Japan, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Australia, India, and Singapore, and of course has a thriving, worldwide community of remote employees.
Amongst our customers are some of the world's most recognizable brands across diverse industries—brands like Toyota, Heineken, Bosch, KeyBank, and UCLA. These customers are the reason we have a 4.6 star rating on G2. Their success is ours, and their stories demonstrate tangible ROI and transformational impact. We are a 9x Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for Low-Code Application Platforms and a multi-year leader in the Forrester Wave. We’re recognized not just as leaders but as visionaries with a strong ability to execute, now extending our leadership into the AI and agentic application development arena.
Working at OutSystems
Our goal is to ensure that OutSystems is a place for bright, happy, and motivated people who share a common purpose and take pride in doing excellent work to pursue our vision of providing the AI-powered low-code development platform enterprise leaders trust to build, secure, and evolve their business applications, agents, and core systems. Our culture is focused on our core values of trust, customer success, innovation, and alignment. Our team members operate with transparency, integrity, and accountability, define success through the lens of the outcomes we deliver for our customers, push the boundaries with excellence, and work together toward our shared vision to deliver on what matters most.
What do we have to offer you?
•
A company that is always growing, changing, and innovating. We challenge each other to innovate in our products, in our team, and how we use our own technology. And we give our teams space to be proactive and creative.
•
Real career opportunities. We care about growth and development. Yes, vertical career progression is a possibility, but it's not the only one. From lateral moves and joining different teams to mastering specialized skills, we support your growth no matter what your goals are.
•
Work colleagues that are as smart, hard-working, and driven as you. We act as one global OutSystems team, taking ownership and working together toward a shared vision.
•
Disrupting the status quo is in our DNA. In fact, it’s why our company exists.
•
We ask “why” a lot. It helps us connect our individual work to the bigger picture and sometimes even uncover a better way.
Are you ready for the next step in your career? Then we’d love to hear from you!
OutSystems nurtures an inclusive culture of diversity, where everyone feels empowered to be their authentic self and perform at their best. Compensation programs that recognize high performance.

A variety of benefits dependent on role and location.

Lead complex analytical projects from scientific planning through execution, ensuring objectives, timelines, quality and regulatory expectations are met.

Develop, optimise and troubleshoot analytical methods for therapeutic proteins, with a particular focus on LC-MS/MS-based characterisation, alongside techniques such as RP, SEC and icIEF.

Apply mass spectrometry to investigate protein primary structure, molecular size, charge variants and post-translational modifications, interpreting complex datasets to generate scientifically robust conclusions.

Perform and technically review analytical testing supporting product characterisation, reference standards and biochemical comparability studies, ensuring results are scientifically sound and appropriately documented.
•
Collaborate with internal teams and external customers, communicating scientific findings clearly and demonstrating Lonza’s expertise in analytical characterisation.

Drive continuous improvement by developing more efficient approaches, supporting non-standard molecules, contributing to root cause investigations and maintaining analytical capabilities in line with industry and regulatory expectations.

Essential: significant hands-on experience with mass spectrometry, particularly LC-MS/MS, applied to protein or biotherapeutic characterisation. This is a non-negotiable requirement.

Proven practical experience developing, validating, optimising and troubleshooting analytical methods for proteins, including LC-based techniques such as RP and SEC; experience with capillary electrophoresis/icIEF is highly desirable.

Experience using LC-MS/MS to characterise protein primary structure, size, charge variants and/or post-translational modifications, with the ability to critically assess and interpret MS data.

Strong understanding of protein chemistry and the regulatory expectations relevant to therapeutic protein characterisation and biochemical comparability studies.

Demonstrated ability to lead complex scientific projects, investigate technical problems and perform effective root cause analysis while maintaining high standards of quality and scientific integrity.

Proven experience mentoring, training or developing junior scientists, particularly in the practical use of LC-MS and analytical characterisation techniques.

Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the confidence to contribute to scientific discussions, guide project teams and communicate effectively with customers and stakeholders.

Shape the Future Through Insight
At Capital Group, our mission is to improve people’s lives through successful investing. Our Capital Associates Program (CAP) invites exceptional early-career talent who combine deep curiosity, analytical rigor, collaborative leadership, and independent thinking to help us explore some of the world’s most complex and consequential investment questions.
CAP is a highly selective, immersive global rotation program for those who want to think deeply, challenge assumptions, and develop the judgment and skills to build a long-term career in investing.
A Truly Differentiated Experience
As a CAP Associate, you will investigate complex investment questions that require original insight, careful judgment, and the ability to synthesize information across industries, markets and disciplines.
The emphasis is on rigorous research: examining industries, assessing long-term trends, asking thoughtful questions, and developing well-reasoned perspectives when answers are rarely obvious. You’ll share your own research approach, explore ideas in depth, and produce thoughtful analyses that contribute to Capital Group’s long-term investment thinking.
CAP Associates have recently researched and presented recommendations/insights on:
• Data Centers in Space
• Valuation Frameworks for Bitcoin and Gold
• Emerging Market Debt in North Macedonia, Albania and Montenegro
• The Lifecycle of U.S. Apparel and Footwear Brands
• Growth of Indian Quick-Service Restaurant Industry
• Quantum Computing Supply Chain and Implications for CMOS Manufacturing
• Japan Satellite Companies
• Potential Applications of Hydrogen in Decarbonizing Mobility
• Energy Storage and Global Lithium
These aren’t hypothetical exercises. CAP Associates explore real-world investment questions and contribute differentiated insights to our investment dialogue.

• Develop Through Practice: Strengthen your analytical reasoning, investigative approach, judgment, and communication skills through hands-on research, close collaboration with investor mentors, and targeted development sessions.
• Learn Alongside Experienced Investors: Work closely with analysts and portfolio managers to understand how rigorous inquiry, qualitative and quantitative analyses, and independent thinking contribute to investment decisions.
• Join a Global Community of Thinkers: Join a small, high-caliber cohort of Associates across London, Los Angeles, and Singapore united by intellectual curiosity and an interest in investing.
Who Should Apply?
We welcome applications from undergraduate or master’s (non-MBA) students in their final year of study and those with up to one year of related experience after graduation.
When we hire for CAP, we look for potential. Strong candidates demonstrate:
• Analytical Rigor and Learning Agility: The ability to absorb new ideas quickly, interrogate assumptions, work through complex problems, and develop well-supported insights.
• Academic Excellence: A record of consistently strong academic achievement. Quantitative skills, double majors, minors, interdisciplinary study and intellectual exploration are valued.
• Adaptability and High Performance: Comfort navigating ambiguity, openness to feedback, and a track record of pursuing demanding goals across academics, work, leadership, or independent interests.
• Collaborative Leadership: The ability to lead, influence, listen, and contribute within teams across academic, professional, or extracurricular settings.
• An Investing Mindset: Demonstrated curiosity about investing and a genuine interest in developing a long-term career as an investor.
• A Distinctive Perspective: Experiences, interests, expertise, or ways of thinking that can contribute to differentiated investment insight.

Job Title
Senior Manager, Prudential Risk
Job Description
So, who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in
established businesses.

Join us at IG – the future gets built here
Your Team:
This is a technically demanding, high-visibility role at the core of IG's second line of defence. As Senior Manager, Prudential Risk, you will be IG's in-house expert on capital adequacy and prudential regulation — owning the ICARA process end-to-end and ensuring IG's regulatory submissions to the FCA meet the highest standards of rigour.
Working in close partnership with Finance and the wider Risk function, you will translate complex regulatory requirements into well-governed capital planning processes. This is a role for a rare combination: quantitative capability, regulatory fluency, and the credibility to engage confidently with the FCA, senior management, and Board-level committees.
What you'll do:
ICARA Process Execution
• Own and execute IG's Internal Capital Adequacy and Risk Assessment (ICARA) process end-to-end, coordinating risk assessments, wind-down analysis, and capital and liquidity adequacy assessments across the Group.
• Design and run stress testing programmes that credibly challenge IG's capital position under a range of macroeconomic, market, and idiosyncratic scenarios.
• Produce the ICARA document to a standard that withstands FCA scrutiny, incorporating clear narrative, robust quantitative analysis, and well-evidenced conclusions.
• Drive continuous improvement of the ICARA methodology, embedding lessons from regulatory feedback and evolving best practice.
Capital Modelling & Quantitative Methodology
• Develop and maintain IG's capital models, covering Pillar 1 own funds requirements, Pillar 2 add-ons, and operational risk capital quantification.
• Build and refine quantitative risk methodologies, including scenario analysis frameworks, tail loss modelling, and sensitivity analysis tools.
• Maintain model documentation to the standard required for internal governance and regulatory review, ensuring assumptions, limitations, and calibration are clearly articulated.
• Monitor MIFIDPRU developments and FCA thematic reviews, assessing implications for IG's capital models and ensuring methodologies remain current.
Regulatory Submissions & Engagement
• Prepare regulatory submissions and associated documentation for FCA requirements, including ICARA submissions, regulatory returns, and responses to supervisory requests.
• Act as subject matter expert during regulatory examinations and thematic reviews, presenting IG's capital assessment approach with clarity and authority.
• Draft IG's responses to FCA consultations relevant to prudential regulation, identifying practical implications and setting out well-reasoned positions.
• Maintain current knowledge of MIFIDPRU, CRD/CRR developments, and FCA supervisory priorities, translating requirements into actionable internal guidance.
Capital Planning & Finance Partnership
• Partner closely with Finance on capital planning, forecasting, and ongoing monitoring, ensuring risk and finance perspectives are well integrated in IG's capital management process.
• Produce regular capital adequacy MI for Risk Committee and Board, providing clear analysis of headroom, sensitivities, and emerging risks to the capital position.
• Support strategic initiatives and M&A activity by providing capital impact assessments and scenario modelling as required.
• Contribute to wind-down planning and recovery analysis, ensuring capital and liquidity adequacy under stress is well-evidenced and clearly documented.
Key Deliverables & Outcomes
• An ICARA process and document that is robust, well-governed, and consistently meets FCA expectations.
• Capital models and quantitative methodologies that are credible, well-documented, and subject to appropriate governance.
• Regulatory submissions of the highest quality, produced on time and to standard.
• A stress testing programme that provides genuine insight into IG's capital resilience across a range of scenarios.
• Strong, trusted relationships with Finance enabling integrated and forward-looking capital planning.
• Clear, actionable capital adequacy MI that supports informed decision-making at committee and Board level.
What you'll need:
Professional Experience
• Significant experience in prudential risk, capital management, or a related quantitative risk discipline within financial services, gained in a second-line, regulatory, or specialist advisory capacity.
• Deep, hands-on knowledge of MIFIDPRU and the ICARA process, including capital adequacy assessment, wind-down analysis, and stress testing.
• Proven track record of developing and maintaining capital models and quantitative risk methodologies, with strong model governance practices.
• Experience preparing regulatory submissions and engaging directly with the FCA or PRA on prudential matters.
• Demonstrated ability to partner with Finance on capital planning and forecasting processes.
• A relevant professional qualification (e.g. CFA, FRM, ACA, or equivalent) is advantageous but not essential.
Skills & Attributes
• Quantitatively strong — comfortable building and stress-testing models, interpreting outputs critically, and communicating uncertainty with appropriate nuance.
• Regulatory fluency — able to navigate complex rulebooks and translate technical requirements into clear, practical guidance for a business audience.
• Precise communicator — produces written work of the quality required for regulatory submission and Board-level consumption.
• Commercially aware — understands business drivers and calibrates capital assessments to reflect real-world constraints and strategic priorities.
• Collaborative and influential — builds trusted cross-functional relationships, particularly with Finance, and operates effectively without direct authority.
• Follows IG's five performance principles: Lead and Inspire, Think Big, Champion the Client, Deliver at Pace, and Raise the Bar.
Why IG Group:
Technical Depth & Regulatory Relevance: Own a genuinely complex prudential risk remit at a regulated FTSE 100 firm, with direct FCA engagement and high visibility across Risk and Finance leadership.
Strategic Consequence: Your capital analysis and ICARA outputs feed directly into Board-level decisions on capital deployment and regulatory standing — a role where analytical quality has real business impact.

The opportunity
Make Unity run everywhere! That is the mantra of the Embedded OS Platforms team. Users expect stunning interactive experiences everywhere: from in-car infotainment systems and digital cockpits to touch-screen kiosks in showrooms and at sporting events. Unity is at the forefront with our scalable, performant runtime engine and Unity Editor workflow.

As UX evolves to include multiple screens, layering of 3D content with other applications and rich multi-touch input, our platform grows to match expectations.

In your first 3-6 months, you've ramped up on one of our embedded platforms, shipped your first integrations and bug fixes, and become a trusted contributor in customer-facing investigations.

Genuinely hard problems at the frontier of Real Time 3D and embedded systems. Contribution to cutting edge automotive HMI experiences. Job Description
About the role
We are looking for a curious and thoughtful UX Researcher with strong foundations in social or behavioural science. This role is well suited to someone who wants to apply rigorous research to complex, real-world problems and grow their career in applied UX research.
You may already have some experience in UX or product research. Equally, you may be completing a PhD, working in academia, government, policy, behavioural research or another applied research environment and looking to move into industry.
What matters most is how you think: asking good questions, challenging assumptions, evaluating evidence critically, designing thoughtful research and turning complex findings into a clear point of view.
What you'll do
Frame complex problems
•
Work with stakeholders to turn broad product or business questions into clear, answerable research questions.
•
Identify assumptions, gaps in knowledge and areas of uncertainty before recommending new research.
•
Review existing evidence and understand user behaviour within its wider social, organisational and technological context.
•
Look beyond individual features to understand workflows, systems and broader patterns.
Design and conduct rigorous research
•
Select research methods that fit the question and the decision being made.
•
Plan and conduct qualitative research such as interviews, contextual inquiry, observation, field research and usability studies.
•
Design studies that consider bias, validity, ethics and the limitations of the available evidence.
•
Adapt research approaches to complex environments and populations that may be difficult to access.
•
Use quantitative approaches where appropriate, including surveys, structured studies and analysis of behavioural or product data to help answer research questions and measure user outcomes.
•
Partner with other researchers and specialists when a project requires different methodological expertise.
Make sense of evidence
•
Analyse qualitative data systematically and identify meaningful patterns.
•
Analyse and interpret quantitative data alongside qualitative findings, identifying patterns and relationships while being clear about sample size, uncertainty and the limitations of the evidence.
•
Distinguish between evidence, interpretation and assumption.
•
Connect individual findings to broader product, user and strategic questions.
Influence decisions
•

PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here
PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges.
About AI for Health
PATH’s Artificial Intelligence (AI) Initiative is our flagship technical team working across divisions to deliver best-in-class evaluation and implementation of AI in health, spanning model evaluation to product development and service innovation. We aim to use AI to address the world’s largest health inequities.
We’re looking for a research engineer to build and run evaluation pipelines that PATH will use to test whether different AI models and products can provide safe and effective mental health/wellbeing support for those most in need. This will include developing simulated users, grounded in data from South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, and the UK, and automated (LLM) judges to score simulated conversations against behaviours defined by local clinicians and lived experience experts. You will implement, maintain, and execute these pipelines in collaboration with leading AI evaluation labs. You’ll also contribute to tool development and support research across PATH’s AI portfolio, and, where time allows, lead research projects of your own.
If you’re a computer scientist and skilled engineer, with experience doing cutting-edge AI research, who wants your work to change how AI is built and used for (mental) health, then this is the role for you!
Responsibilities:
Build and Run Benchmarking Pipelines
• Contribute your expertise to deliver efficient and accurate AI evaluation design in global (mental) health.
• Run AI evaluations at scale: create and sample simulated users to hold single- and multi-session conversations with AI models and products, scoring transcripts with automated judges, and gathering results for analysis and publication.
• Work closely with our technical partners (e.g., Transluce, Digital Umuganda) to adapt and co-develop tooling for user simulation, LLM-judging, validation etc. to the countries, languages, models, and products we aim to evaluate.
• Keep our results traceable, reproducible, and (research) publication ready.
Develop Tools
• Help build and maintain tools across our work, such as tooling for user simulation or for integrating local expert input to improve evaluation accuracy.
• Write well-tested, documented code for open release, and prepare our tooling for long-term stewardship by partner organizations.
• Share knowledge and expertise with our partners and other stakeholders in the countries where we work so that they can learn how to use our tools to perform their own evaluations.
Support Research across the Portfolio
• Support PATH’s AI for Health team to deliver research by contributing ideas, methods, engineering support, and technical expertise.
• Where time allows, lead discrete research projects of your own, and publish the results.
• This is a full-time post based in London. You’ll report to PATH’s Deputy Director for AI for Health and work closely with our technical partners. This role includes occasional international travel (around 5% of time).
Required Skills and Experience
• BSc or MSc in computer science, software engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
• Strong Python skills, with a record of writing well-tested, maintainable code (version control, code review, automated testing, continuous integration).
• Proven experience evaluating artificial intelligence models, e.g., an evaluation pipeline, or similar large-scale contributions to research.
• Experience with cloud infrastructure, containers, and data pipelines (e.g., AWS, GCP, or Azure; Docker).
• Ability to work independently with external technical partners, and to explain technical work clearly to clinical, research, and policy colleagues.
• Ability to handle sensitive data, including mental health content, with care.
Preferred Skills & Experience
• Understanding of the current AI safety literature, and an interest in topics relevant to alignment with positive health outcomes.
• Experience building or running healthcare-specific AI evaluations or benchmarks.
• Experience automating interaction with web or mobile apps (e.g., with Playwright for end-to-end testing).
• Experience with multilingual NLP.
• Experience contributing to or maintaining open-source software.
• Experience with frontend deployments.

Analog Design Intern – CSS Power Management
Location: Edinburgh, Scotland
Job Description
Analog Devices is seeking an Analog Design Intern – Power Management to join our engineering team in Edinburgh.
The successful candidate will join a collaborative team developing advanced low-power analog and power-management IP for highly integrated mixed-signal ICs. Working alongside experienced analog, mixed-signal and power-management engineers, the intern will contribute to real IC development activities while gaining practical experience in circuit architecture, transistor-level design, modelling, simulation and verification.
The team develops power-management solutions with a strong focus on low-power operation, high efficiency and small solution size. Key areas include switched-mode DC/DC converters such as buck, boost and buck-boost architectures, together with the analog building blocks required for their control, monitoring and protection.
This internship provides an opportunity to apply university knowledge to real silicon designs and develop an understanding of the complete IC development process, from architecture and modelling through circuit implementation, physical design, verification and potentially silicon evaluation.
Responsibilities
• Conduct circuit architecture research and feasibility studies for low-power power-management functions.
• Contribute to the architecture, design, simulation and verification of DC/DC converter IP, including buck, boost and buck-boost topologies.
• Design and analyse analog sub-circuits used within power converters, potentially including error amplifiers, comparators, voltage/current references, oscillators, gate drivers, level shifters, current-sensing circuits and protection functions.
• Develop simulation testbenches and contribute to design verification across process, voltage, temperature and operating-load conditions.
• Analyse important converter performance trade-offs including efficiency, quiescent current, transient response, output ripple, stability, silicon area and external component requirements.
• Explore different converter operating modes and control techniques to optimise efficiency across load conditions.
• Contribute to behavioural and system-level modelling to evaluate converter architectures and control-loop performance.
• Work closely with layout engineers during physical implementation, including review of parasitic effects and layout-dependent performance.
• Participate in technical and design reviews with experienced analog and power-management engineers.
• Support top-level integration and verification of power-management IP within larger mixed-signal systems.
• Where appropriate, contribute to laboratory evaluation and comparison of simulated and measured silicon performance.
Minimum Qualifications
• Currently pursuing a BEng, MEng, MSc or PhD in Electronic/Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics or a closely related discipline.
• Good understanding of fundamental analog electronics and circuit theory.
• Understanding of CMOS devices and basic transistor-level circuit operation.
• Familiarity with feedback systems, frequency response and stability.
• Basic understanding of power electronics and switching circuits.
• Some experience with circuit simulation or electronic design tools through university, personal or industry projects.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Good written and verbal communication skills.
• Enthusiasm for learning and working collaboratively within an engineering team.
Preferred Qualifications
• Understanding of DC/DC converter architectures, particularly buck, boost or buck-boost converters.
• Familiarity with concepts such as PWM/PFM operation, feedback control, loop stability and transient response.
• Familiarity with transistor-level IC design and tools such as Cadence Virtuoso and Spectre.
• Exposure to power-converter modelling or simulation using tools such as SIMPLIS, MATLAB or Simulink.
• Understanding of common power-management building blocks such as LDOs, voltage/current references, comparators, oscillators, current sensing and gate drivers.
• Familiarity with low-power circuit-design techniques and quiescent-current optimisation.
• Experience using laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, power supplies, electronic loads and signal generators.
• Programming or scripting experience using Python, MATLAB or similar tools for modelling, simulation or data analysis.
• A strong interest in analog IC design, power management and energy-efficient electronic systems.

Job Description: Equipment Engineer Wafer Fab and Epitaxy (Continental Shift)
Location: Caswell, Northamptonshire
Reports to: Equipment Engineering Shift Manager
About Lumentum
Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE) is a global leader in innovative optical and photonic products enabling optical networking and commercial laser customers worldwide. Our technologies are integral to virtually every type of telecom, enterprise, and data centre network, and support advanced manufacturing and next generation sensing applications. Lumentum’s UK wafer fabrication facility in Caswell is a centre of excellence for high-performance optoelectronic devices used in telecommunications and industrial systems.
Role Summary
As an Equipment Technician, you will provide technical support for the operation and maintenance of wafer fabrication and epitaxy equipment on a continental shift pattern. This role offers the opportunity to work on advanced III-V semiconductor technologies within a highly specialised UK fabrication facility, supporting products deployed globally in next-generation communications networks. Your primary focus will be the fault diagnosis, repair, and optimisation of advanced semiconductor process tools including vacuum, pneumatic, mechanical, electrical, and RF systems, as well as equipment handling hazardous process gases and chemicals.
This is a hands-on, high-precision engineering role ideal for those with experience maintaining complex electro-mechanical systems in critical environments including high-tech manufacturing, aerospace, defence, or UK Armed Forces technical trades.
Key Responsibilities
• Provide rapid first-line engineering response to minimise tool downtime and production impact.
• Conduct repairs, fault diagnosis and preventative maintenance on semiconductor processing equipment including, but not limited to lithography, etch, PVD, PECVD and MOVPE reactor systems.
• Manage chemical and specialty gas supply systems in compliance with statutory, site safety and environmental standards.
• Support maintenance of gas delivery, exhaust and abatement systems associated with epitaxy and PECVD tools.
• Manage spare parts inventory to ensure availability of critical components and minimise downtime.
• Implement and support preventative maintenance strategies to maximise OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) and uptime.
• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives (Kaizen, 6S, 8D) and maintain accurate documentation of actions and outcomes.
• Participate in production and planning meetings to represent equipment engineering performance.
• Support the site emergency response function including participation in the Site Emergency Response Team.
• Fork-lift truck operation will be required (training will be provided).
Key Relationships
• Process and Equipment Engineering Teams
• Facilities and Maintenance Teams
• Manufacturing Operations Team
• MES (PROMIS) and IT Teams
Qualifications
Apprenticeship, HNC, HND or Degree in an Electrical or Mechanical Engineering discipline (or equivalent). Alternatively, a minimum of 5 years’ directly relevant experience in complex electro-mechanical system maintenance.
Preferred Backgrounds and Transferable Skills
We actively welcome applications from engineers with experience in high-reliability environments such as aerospace, defence, automotive manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, oil & gas, power generation, or UK Armed Forces technical trades. Direct semiconductor experience is advantageous but not essential.
Skills
Essential:
• Proven experience in a high-tech, precision-engineering environment.
• Strong fault-finding and diagnostic ability across electrical, electronic and mechanical systems.
• Ability to work safely with hazardous gases and chemicals.
• Ability to follow detailed documented procedures with minimal supervision.
• Competence in documenting procedures, risk assessments, and method statements.
• Effective time management and organisational skills.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
• Team-oriented approach with excellent communication skills.
• Ability to read and interpret technical documentation and communicate effectively within a safety-critical manufacturing environment.
Desirable:
• Previous experience within a semiconductor or cleanroom manufacturing environment.
Other Requirements
• 40.3 hours per week on a continental shift pattern (2 days, 2 nights, 4 off), 12-hour shifts including weekends and bank holidays as part of the continental rotation.
• Work is performed within a cleanroom environment (cleanroom garments provided).
• Role requires use of Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA). Candidates must be able to meet the medical and respiratory protective equipment (RPE) face-fit requirements associated with SCBA use in accordance with site safety standards.
• Must be eligible to work in the UK.
• The Caswell site is located in a rural setting in Northamptonshire. A full UK driving licence and access to own transport are essential.

Bring important trends to the surface, helping the team understand what is changing, why it matters, and where more analysis may be needed.

Replace static, manual reporting with more interactive insight solutions that help users explore trends, compare results, test assumptions, and identify areas for deeper review.

Promote practical and responsible use of AI and analytics, with a focus on improving speed, transparency, and confidence while maintaining strong governance and actuarial judgement.

Help improve how reserving insights are communicated so they are concise, consistent, and useful for actuarial, finance, management, and business discussions.

Help define clear standards for reserving metrics, data definitions, reporting, reconciliation, and interpretation of key indicators.
•
Support high-quality, governed outputs that align with enterprise data standards, actuarial controls, and financial reporting needs.
Collaborate Across D&A
•
Collaborate with architecture, engineering, governance, finance, actuarial, claims, and underwriting colleagues so reserving needs are considered from the data foundation through to the final insight experience.

Look for opportunities to simplify processes, reduce manual data wrangling, and build reusable insight capabilities that teams can rely on over time.

Experience creating dashboards, datasets, visualizations, or self-service tools that help business users understand performance, trends, and drivers.
